title: MGUS, Smoldering Myeloma and Multiple Myeloma: The IMWG Fences
summary: Learn what SPEP, serum immunofixation and serum free light chains each contribute, and how the 3 g/dL, 10% plasma cell, CRAB and biomarker criteria separate MGUS, smoldering myeloma and multiple myeloma, plus how MGUS risk is graded.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 47 Hit 3 (MGUS definition, prevalence, progression, follow-up), Hit 5 (SPEP + serum IFE screening; sFLC ratio ≥100 biomarker), Exam Trap 5 and its MGUS/smoldering/myeloma table (Table 2), and Exam Trap 6 (the <10% fence). Checked against Abeykoon 2022, Lakshman 2018, Mateos 2020 and the IMWG Mass Spectrometry Committee report (Murray 2021). Corrections taught from the sources: MGUS prevalence is ~3% at ≥50 years and ~5% at ≥70 years (the reviewer gives ~3% at ≥70); MGUS also requires M-protein <3 g/dL and smoldering myeloma can be met by M-protein ≥3 g/dL (or urine ≥500 mg/24 h) alone; follow-up intervals differ by guideline (the reviewer’s “every 6–12 months” is not the IMWG low-risk schedule). Not taught (pending): the reviewer’s “IgG ≥2 g/dL, IgA ≥1 g/dL suspicious for malignancy” thresholds, the biopsy-proven plasmacytoma route to myeloma, and sFLC monitoring of light-chain escape. M-spike quantitation (Hit 4) is not taught here.

objectives: State what SPEP, serum immunofixation and the serum free light chain assay each contribute to detecting a monoclonal protein.
Classify a patient as MGUS, smoldering myeloma or multiple myeloma using the M-protein, marrow plasma cell, CRAB and biomarker criteria.
List the three Mayo risk factors for MGUS progression and explain why follow-up advice differs between guidelines.

scenes.title: Three spikes, three labels?
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three patients each have a monoclonal protein (M-protein) on serum protein electrophoresis, and none has hypercalcaemia, renal failure, anaemia or bone lesions. Patient A: IgG kappa 1.2 g/dL, 4% marrow plasma cells, normal free light chain ratio. Patient B: IgA 3.4 g/dL, 12% marrow plasma cells. Patient C: 14% clonal marrow plasma cells, involved kappa free light chain 450 mg/L, involved:uninvolved ratio 150. Question token: “MGUS, smoldering, or myeloma?”

cues.text: Invented scenario: three patients each have a monoclonal spike on serum protein electrophoresis, and none has calcium, kidney, blood count or bone damage.

Patient A has a small IgG spike and few marrow plasma cells. Patient B has a large IgA spike and twelve percent plasma cells. Patient C has fourteen percent plasma cells and a free light chain ratio of one hundred fifty.
No organ damage in any of them. Are they all the same diagnosis?

props.label: No CRAB damage in any of them

scenes.title: Finding and naming the M-protein
scenes.altText: Three test cards. Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) detects the M-protein and gives its relative quantity. Serum immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE) establishes its isotype (heavy chain and kappa or lambda light chain). Serum free light chain (sFLC) assay quantifies free kappa and free lambda; a kappa:lambda ratio below 0.26 or above 1.65 suggests a clone, but not every myeloma has an abnormal ratio; sFLC is especially useful in AL amyloidosis and nonsecretory myeloma. Panel token: an IMWG panel (2009) concluded SPEP + serum IFE + sFLC should be used together for screening. Epidemiology token: MGUS in about 3% of people aged 50 or older and about 5% aged 70 or older; progression about 1% per year.

cues.text: Three tests work together. Serum protein electrophoresis detects the monoclonal protein and gives its relative amount. Immunofixation names its isotype: the heavy chain, and kappa or lambda.

The serum free light chain assay measures free kappa and free lambda. A kappa to lambda ratio below 0.26 or above 1.65 suggests a clone, but not every myeloma has an abnormal ratio. It is especially useful in amyloidosis and nonsecretory myeloma.
A 2009 International Myeloma Working Group panel concluded that the three should be used together for screening: electrophoresis, serum immunofixation, and free light chains.

A spike with fewer than ten percent clonal plasma cells and no damage is MGUS, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance. It is found in about three percent of people aged fifty or older and about five percent at seventy or older, and progresses at roughly one percent a year.

props.label: Screen: SPEP + serum IFE + sFLC together
MGUS: ~3% at ≥ 50 y · ~5% at ≥ 70 y · ~1%/year progress

scenes.title: The fences: 3 g/dL, 10%, and damage
scenes.altText: Three criteria cards (IMWG 2014). MGUS: serum M-protein below 3 g/dL, clonal marrow plasma cells below 10%, and no end-organ damage attributable to the clone. Smoldering myeloma: M-protein 3 g/dL or more (or urine M-protein 500 mg/24 h or more) and/or clonal marrow plasma cells 10% or more, with no CRAB damage and no myeloma-defining biomarker. Multiple myeloma: clonal marrow plasma cells 10% or more plus a myeloma-defining event, either CRAB damage or a biomarker. CRAB card: calcium above 11 mg/dL or more than 1 mg/dL above the upper limit; creatinine clearance below 40 mL/min or creatinine above 2 mg/dL; haemoglobin below 10 g/dL or more than 2 g/dL below the lower limit; osteolytic lesions on imaging. Biomarker card: clonal marrow plasma cells 60% or more; involved:uninvolved sFLC ratio 100 or more with involved FLC at least 100 mg/L; more than one focal lesion on MRI.

cues.text: Now the fences. MGUS needs all three: an M-protein under three grams per decilitre, clonal marrow plasma cells under ten percent, and no end-organ damage from the clone.

Smoldering myeloma crosses a fence but causes no damage: an M-protein of three grams or more, or a urine M-protein of five hundred milligrams a day or more, or ten percent or more plasma cells, or both.

Damage means CRAB. Calcium above eleven, or over one above the upper limit. Creatinine clearance below forty, or creatinine above two. Haemoglobin below ten, or over two below the lower limit. Lytic bone lesions.

Since 2014, three biomarkers also define myeloma without CRAB, in a patient with at least ten percent clonal plasma cells: sixty percent or more plasma cells, a free light chain ratio of one hundred or more with the involved chain at least one hundred milligrams per litre, or more than one focal lesion on MRI.

scenes.title: Labelling the three patients
scenes.altText: Hook answers. A: M-protein 1.2 g/dL and 4% plasma cells, no damage: MGUS. B: M-protein 3.4 g/dL and 12% plasma cells, no damage or biomarker: smoldering myeloma. C: 14% clonal plasma cells with sFLC ratio 150 and involved FLC 450 mg/L: multiple myeloma by biomarker, even without CRAB. Risk card (Mayo model): three risk factors for MGUS progression are an abnormal FLC ratio, a non-IgG isotype, and M-protein 1.5 g/dL or more; patient A has none (low risk). Follow-up card: guidance differs between groups; the IMWG recommendation summarised by Abeykoon 2022 is a recheck at 6 months, then every 2–3 years if stable for low risk, or yearly for higher risk.

cues.text: Back to the hook. Patient A: a small spike, four percent plasma cells, no damage. That is MGUS. Patient B crosses both fences without damage: smoldering myeloma.

Patient C has no CRAB, but has fourteen percent clonal plasma cells and a light chain ratio of one hundred fifty with the involved chain well above one hundred milligrams per litre. That biomarker makes it multiple myeloma.

MGUS itself carries graded risk. The Mayo model counts three factors: an abnormal free light chain ratio, a non-IgG isotype, and an M-protein of one point five grams or more. Patient A has none, so is low risk.
Follow-up advice differs between expert groups. The working group suggests a recheck at six months, then every two to three years if a low-risk patient is stable, or yearly for higher risk.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Under 10% marrow plasma cells means MGUS” (✓ MGUS also needs M-protein under 3 g/dL and no damage; 3 g/dL or more is smoldering); “No CRAB means no myeloma” (✓ since 2014 a biomarker can define myeloma); “A free light chain ratio of 100 or more is myeloma by itself” (✓ it counts only with 10% or more clonal plasma cells and involved FLC at least 100 mg/L).

cues.text: Trap one: under ten percent plasma cells means MGUS. Not alone: the M-protein must also be under three grams, with no damage. Three grams or more is smoldering myeloma.
Trap two: no CRAB means no myeloma. Since 2014, sixty percent plasma cells, a light chain ratio of one hundred, or more than one MRI lesion can define myeloma.
Trap three: a ratio of one hundred is myeloma by itself. It counts with at least ten percent clonal plasma cells and an involved light chain of at least one hundred milligrams per litre.

scenes.title: Three, ten, then the trigger
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “THREE and TEN are the fences; CRAB or a biomarker is the trigger. Inside both fences with no trigger = MGUS. Over a fence, no trigger = smoldering. Clone of 10% or more plus a trigger = myeloma.” Tokens: 3 g/dL · 10% · trigger. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: three and ten are the fences, and CRAB or a biomarker is the trigger. Inside both fences with no trigger is MGUS. Over a fence with no trigger is smoldering. A clone of ten percent or more plus a trigger is myeloma.
Where it breaks: IgM and light-chain MGUS have their own definitions; the light chain trigger needs the involved chain at one hundred milligrams per litre; and risk rises gradually, not at one line.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “M-protein < 3 g/dL + clonal PCs < 10% + no damage = MGUS · over a fence, no damage = smoldering”, “Clonal PCs ≥ 10% + CRAB or biomarker (60% · FLC ratio ≥ 100 · > 1 MRI lesion) = myeloma”.

cues.text: An M-protein under 3 grams per decilitre with under ten percent marrow plasma cells and no damage is MGUS, crossing either fence without damage is smoldering myeloma, and adding CRAB damage or a myeloma-defining biomarker makes it multiple myeloma.

props.label: < 3 g/dL + PCs < 10% + no damage = MGUS · over a fence = smoldering

explanation.what: Plain language: a single clone of plasma cells can make one antibody in excess (the M-protein). How big the spike is, how many plasma cells sit in the marrow, and whether the clone is damaging organs decides whether this is a watch-and-wait precursor or cancer needing treatment. Scientific terms: monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM), multiple myeloma (MM), serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP), serum immunofixation electrophoresis (IFE), serum free light chain (sFLC) assay and κ/λ ratio, CRAB features, myeloma-defining biomarkers (International Myeloma Working Group, IMWG 2014).
explanation.why: Ultra-high-risk smoldering myeloma (marrow plasma cells ≥60%, sFLC ratio ≥100, >1 MRI focal lesion) had about an 80% risk of progression within 2 years, so the IMWG reclassified it as myeloma to allow treatment before organ damage. Most MGUS never progresses, so risk factors guide how closely to follow it.
explanation.measure: MGUS: M-protein <3 g/dL, clonal marrow plasma cells <10%, no end-organ damage. SMM: M-protein ≥3 g/dL (or urine ≥500 mg/24 h) and/or clonal marrow plasma cells ≥10%, no CRAB, no biomarker. MM: clonal marrow plasma cells ≥10% plus CRAB (calcium >11 mg/dL or >1 mg/dL above ULN; CrCl <40 mL/min or creatinine >2 mg/dL; Hb <10 g/dL or >2 g/dL below LLN; osteolytic lesions) or a biomarker (≥60% plasma cells; involved:uninvolved sFLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L; >1 MRI focal lesion). Normal κ/λ FLC ratio 0.26–1.65. Mayo MGUS risk factors: abnormal FLC ratio, non-IgG isotype, M-protein ≥1.5 g/dL.
explanation.differs: SPEP (detects and quantifies) vs IFE (isotypes) vs sFLC (free κ and λ, ratio); MGUS vs SMM (crossing the 3 g/dL or 10% fence) vs MM (CRAB or biomarker); MGUS risk factors (graded follow-up) vs myeloma-defining events (diagnosis).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: classify a patient from M-protein, marrow plasma cell percentage, CRAB and FLC values; recognise that a biomarker can define myeloma without CRAB; pick the screening panel; name the MGUS risk factors.

comparisons.title: MGUS vs smoldering myeloma

right.label: Smoldering myeloma
points: M-protein ≥ 3 g/dL or urine ≥ 500 mg/24 h

comparisons.distinguisher: Whether either fence (3 g/dL or 10%) is crossed.

comparisons.title: Smoldering vs multiple myeloma

right.label: Multiple myeloma
points: PCs ≥ 60%, FLC ratio ≥ 100 or > 1 MRI lesion

comparisons.distinguisher: A myeloma-defining event: CRAB or one of the three biomarkers.

mnemonic.text: THREE and TEN are the fences; CRAB or a biomarker is the trigger. Inside both fences with no trigger = MGUS. Over a fence, no trigger = smoldering. Clone of 10% or more plus a trigger = myeloma.
mnemonic.explanation: Separates the two size fences (M-protein 3 g/dL, marrow plasma cells 10%) from the damage or biomarker trigger.
mnemonic.limitation: IgM and light-chain MGUS have their own definitions; the light-chain biomarker needs involved FLC ≥100 mg/L as well as ratio ≥100; the plasmacytoma route to myeloma is not covered; progression risk rises gradually rather than at one cut-off.

analogyLimitations: Criteria shown as schematic cards; no electrophoresis images.
The fence-and-trigger picture simplifies graded risk into categories.
takeaway: An M-protein under 3 grams per decilitre with under ten percent marrow plasma cells and no damage is MGUS, crossing either fence without damage is smoldering myeloma, and adding CRAB damage or a myeloma-defining biomarker makes it multiple myeloma.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old has an IgG kappa M-protein of 2.1 g/dL and 6% clonal bone marrow plasma cells. Calcium, creatinine and haemoglobin are normal and imaging shows no lytic lesions. Which classification fits?

options.rationale: Correct. M-protein below 3 g/dL, clonal plasma cells below 10% and no end-organ damage meet all three MGUS criteria.
Incorrect. Smoldering myeloma needs an M-protein of 3 g/dL or more or 10% or more clonal plasma cells; neither is present.

options.text: Multiple myeloma, because an M-protein above 2 g/dL indicates malignancy
options.rationale: Incorrect. Myeloma needs 10% or more clonal plasma cells plus CRAB damage or a biomarker; a 2.1 g/dL M-protein is a Mayo risk factor (1.5 g/dL or more), not a diagnostic criterion.

options.text: Multiple myeloma, because IgG kappa is the commonest myeloma isotype
options.rationale: Incorrect. Isotype does not define the diagnosis; the M-protein size, marrow plasma cells and damage do.

questions.stem: A patient has 30% clonal bone marrow plasma cells and an M-protein of 2.5 g/dL, with no hypercalcaemia, renal impairment, anaemia or bone lesions. The involved:uninvolved serum free light chain ratio is 140, with involved FLC 600 mg/L. Under the 2014 IMWG criteria, what is the diagnosis?

options.text: Multiple myeloma defined by a biomarker
options.rationale: Correct. With at least 10% clonal plasma cells, an sFLC ratio of 100 or more with involved FLC at least 100 mg/L is a myeloma-defining event even without CRAB.

options.text: High-risk smoldering myeloma, because there is no CRAB damage
options.rationale: Incorrect. Since 2014, patients with this biomarker are reclassified from smoldering myeloma to myeloma.

options.text: MGUS, because the M-protein is below 3 g/dL
options.rationale: Incorrect. MGUS also requires fewer than 10% clonal plasma cells; this patient has 30%.

options.text: No diagnosis can be made until organ damage develops
options.rationale: Incorrect. The biomarker criteria exist so that myeloma can be diagnosed before CRAB damage.

questions.stem: Which combination did an International Myeloma Working Group panel recommend for screening for a monoclonal plasma cell disorder?

options.text: Serum protein electrophoresis, serum immunofixation and serum free light chains
options.rationale: Correct. The 2009 IMWG panel concluded that the three tests should be used together for screening.
Incorrect. Electrophoresis detects and quantifies the spike but does not establish its isotype.

options.text: Serum free light chain ratio alone
options.rationale: Incorrect. Not every patient with myeloma has an abnormal free light chain ratio at diagnosis.
Incorrect. Immunofixation establishes the isotype, while electrophoresis gives the quantity; the panel also adds free light chains.

claims.text: Roles of SPEP, serum IFE and sFLC; FLC ratio range; 2009 IMWG screening panel.
MGUS criteria (M-protein <3 g/dL, plasma cells <10%, no end-organ damage) and CRAB definitions.
Myeloma-defining biomarkers (≥60% plasma cells; FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L; >1 MRI focal lesion) in patients with ≥10% clonal plasma cells; ~80% 2-year progression rationale.
MGUS prevalence ~3% at ≥50 and ~5% at ≥70 years; progression ~1%/year.
Mayo MGUS risk factors: abnormal FLC ratio, non-IgG isotype, M-protein ≥1.5 g/dL.
Follow-up recommendations differ between groups; IMWG: 6 months, then every 2–3 years (low risk) or yearly (higher risk).
Reviewer: M-spikes of IgG ≥2 g/dL or IgA ≥1 g/dL are suspicious for malignancy. Not found in the sources read; not taught.
Biopsy-proven plasmacytoma as an alternative to ≥10% plasma cells for myeloma; serial sFLC for light-chain escape and oligosecretory myeloma. Not verified; not taught.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 47 Hit 3 says MGUS is present in ~3% of people ≥70. Abeykoon 2022 (citing Kyle 2006, Olmsted County) gives ~3% at ≥50 and ~5% at ≥70 (3.2% and 5.3%). The lesson teaches the source figures (register flag rv-mgus-prevalence-age).

Ch. 47 Hit 3 says to follow MGUS with SPEP every 6–12 months. Abeykoon 2022 shows that follow-up advice differs by guideline and risk; the IMWG suggests 6 months, then every 2–3 years for stable low-risk MGUS, or yearly for higher risk (register flag rv-mgus-followup-interval).

Ch. 47 Hit 3 says M-spikes of IgG ≥2 g/dL or IgA ≥1 g/dL are suspicious for malignancy. The sources read use M-protein ≥1.5 g/dL and non-IgG isotype as MGUS progression risk factors and 3 g/dL as the MGUS/SMM fence; the reviewer thresholds were not found and are not taught (register flag rv-mgus-mspike-threshold).

Ch. 47 Exam Trap 6 and the MGUS/smoldering/myeloma table use only the <10% plasma cell fence. Under IMWG criteria (Abeykoon 2022; Lakshman 2018) MGUS also needs M-protein <3 g/dL, and smoldering myeloma is met by M-protein ≥3 g/dL (or urine ≥500 mg/24 h) even with <10% plasma cells (register flag rv-mgus-smm-mprotein-fence).
